geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the broad courtyard with a smaller access-aligned notch to strengthen the public threshold without destabilizing the dominant stepped bar.
Align the opening to the verified access edge in the program frame.
Limit the carve so the mass remains dominant and capacity-aware.
Make the entry void legible at ground level.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the current courtyard into a smaller, more legible public entry carve so the verified access edge reads as an active threshold rather than a generic internal void.
Bind the carved entry to the program-frame access side already indicated by the design concept graph.
Keep the opening bounded and architectural rather than turning the whole mass into a large subtraction.
Create a readable ground-level seam with enough height to register as an entry void.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent stepped bar in all four views, so it clears the coherence gate and does not visibly self-collide across views. The dominant gesture is clear: a compact linear mass with successive upper setbacks. The green parcel is respected, and the mass sits as an interior occupancy rather than merely filling the box. However, the public-space figure is weak: the blue frontage edge is acknowledged only minimally, with no strong court, undercut, or entry seam evident at the access side. That makes the neighborhood-living brief plausible but under-articulated at ground level. The section is acceptable as calm upper massing, but it behaves more like a generic stepped extrusion than a fully program-clarifying mixed-use threshold. Overall this is program-fit enough to pass, but it would benefit from a clearer carved/public ground condition on the access edge.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is much lower and more bar-like; do not copy the tower scale or the dramatic skyline context.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/terraced massing can stay coherent when one dominant volume is legible and upper setbacks read as a single capacity-bearing section.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is more vertical and office-like than the candidate; only the sectional continuity principle transfers.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A tall mass can retain continuity through a slightly torqued or tapered upper profile while preserving a stable base.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is single-story and frontage-driven; the candidate is more volumetric and stepped, so only the active-edge logic transfers.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact street object can support neighborhood program when it clearly marks a public threshold and ground-edge event.

warnings: Frontage response is present but subdued; consider a more legible entry seam or notch aligned to the verified access edge.
The stepped silhouette is coherent, but it currently reads more as setback code than as an inhabited public section.
Precedent resonance is moderate rather than strong because the candidate lacks a more distinct court/terrace or torqued section principle.
